scope: Proposition 2.2 (Finite oscillation of smooth orbit averages) of the manuscript “Pointwise convergence of triple ergodic averages for mixing transformations” (preprints/Pointwise-convergence-of-triple-ergodic-averages-for-mixing-transformations-October-4-2026/pointwise-triple-ergodic-averages-mixing-transformations.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 154 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e76fd7732f10b250), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 5. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: For every averaging profile φ, there is a constant Cφ < ∞ with the following property. On every invertible probability preserving system, let f1, f2, f3 : X → C be measurable with |fj(x)| ≤ 1 for all x, and define V φ k (x) = X n∈Z φ2k (n) 3 Y j=1 fj(Tjn x), k = 0, 1, 2, . . . . For every integer w ≥ 1 and every deterministic list of integers 0 ≤ k1 < · · · < kw+1, w X i=1 Z X max ki≤ℓ≤ki+1 |V φ ℓ − V φ ki | dµ ≤ Cφ √ w. (2.3) The constant is independent of the system, the inputs, w, and the endpoints.
